summary: Texas-tower light 32 miles off Cape Fear, lit in 1964 to replace a lightship; automated 1979; privately owned since 2010.

access.note: Privately owned (owners' site). The USLHS record says not open to the public; the owners' site says its visitor program has returned, with trips open for booking on its own site.

stay.note: The owners' site says each trip on its calendar is two nights aboard. LighthouseFriends says the new owner plans to offer stays. Visits are arranged directly with the owners.

events.note: Lighthouse Board places a lightship on the shoal; seven lightships serve there to 1930.
New steel light-vessel with a 12-inch steam whistle replaces light-vessel No. 29.
Schooner Minnie stranded on the shoal on April 12, 1882, in a northeast rain storm; the captain had misjudged his position relative to the lightship.
Lightship LV 115 (WAL 537) rode out Hurricane Donna on station, per a crew member's account printed by LighthouseFriends.
Upper part built in Louisiana by J. Ray McDermott Co. and set on four steel legs.
Activated 24 November 1964; the lightship WAL 537 was relieved.
Resident Coast Guard watch gave way to automated operation.
LighthouseFriends gives 2003 (replaced by a large navigational buoy). The owners' site gives 2004 for Coast Guard retirement.
Retired from Coast Guard service, per the owners' site.
General Services Administration auction; Shipwrecks, Inc. high bid $515,000 did not close; a later sealed bid of $11,262 fell below fair market value.
Richard Neal acquired the tower for $85,000 in August 2010.
Auction announced in May 2018 and cancelled in favour of fractional ownership.
Ownership changed in July 2026; LighthouseFriends says the nonprofit sold to new owners, the owners' site says ownership consolidated among existing co-owners.

keepers.name: Oscar B. O'Neal
keepers.note: Headed the station's first six-man crew (LighthouseFriends).

corrections.why: The owners' site says the Coast Guard retired the station from active service in 2004; LighthouseFriends says it was deactivated in 2003 and replaced by a buoy. The USLHS place record still shows an active aid, so this needs a human look.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record gives 2003 (Rowlett, via Wikidata). LighthouseFriends also gives 2003. The owners' site gives 2004 for retirement from Coast Guard service, which is a different event from the end of the light as an aid.

notes_for_editor: Roster: 62 USLHS lines, 8 principal keepers (role head keeper) and 54 USCG lines (role crew, per the archive's 'USCG' heading). Names and years are the archive's; not each confirmed in a primary register. Distances: the sources give miles, not nautical miles, so the story keeps miles and converts nothing. Disagreements stated in the story now also include the owners' visitor programme against the USLHS 'not open to the public' entry, the USLHS 'active aid' entry against the owners' 'no longer an active aid', and FPTower's July 2025 majority-ownership date. Five disagreements were already stated in the story: light height (archive 118 ft above mean high water; owners 135 ft); tower cost ($1.5 million vs $2 million, both LighthouseFriends); deactivation (2003 LighthouseFriends, 2004 owners); auction-to-sale (2009 GSA auction; 2010 sale); and current ownership (LighthouseFriends says the nonprofit sold to new owners; the owners' site says co-owners consolidated; FPTower's own page describes fractional ownership). The owners are not named beyond Richard Neal, who is named in his public role as the 2010 buyer; current owners are not named. The USCG Historian article on this light could not be read (403 direct and via archive). Newspapers: not searched. Hurricane Donna (12 September 1960) rests on a crewman's account printed by LighthouseFriends, which cites Ocean Navigator (March/April 2003); not checked against HURDAT2. The 1932 Maria stranding in LighthouseFriends is left out (no source given). Personal details LighthouseFriends prints about crew and the owner are left out. The corpus has no coverage of the tower itself (its volumes end before 1964 except the Bulletin to 1939). The 1793 to 1854 lightship history rests on LighthouseFriends and the Board volumes. The record's status 'active' is proposed as a correction, not applied.
